name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMISTRY_IN_EVERYDAY_LIFE_MCQ_Q01 - Incorrect statement regarding antiseptic medicines

questiontext.text: Which of the following statements is not correct.

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Antiseptics and disinfectants are both antimicrobial agents that prevent the growth or pathogenic action of microorganisms. Antiseptics are designed for living tissues, whereas disinfectants are formulated for non-living objects.

Step 2: Evaluation of Ingestion
Antiseptics are safe for topical application on living tissues such as cuts, wounds, ulcers, and diseased skin surfaces. Unlike antibiotics, antiseptics are harmful to internal tissues and organs and therefore cannot be ingested.

Step 3: Verification of Cleansing and Dilution Properties
Certain antiseptics (for example, bithionol) are added to soaps to impart antiseptic properties and reduce body odor. Additionally, the concentration of an antimicrobial substance can determine its role; for instance, a 0.2 percent aqueous solution of phenol acts as an antiseptic, whereas a 1.0 percent aqueous solution acts as a disinfectant.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The statement that antiseptic medicines can be ingested is incorrect.

answer.text: Some antiseptics can be added to soaps.
Dilute solutions of some disinfectants can be used as antiseptic.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMISTRY_IN_EVERYDAY_LIFE_MCQ_Q02 - Composition and function of birth control pills

questiontext.text: Which is the correct statement about birth control pills?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Birth control pills belong to the class of antifertility drugs, which control pregnancy through hormonal regulation.

Step 2: Hormonal Mechanism and Composition
Oral contraceptives essentially contain a combination of synthetic estrogen and progesterone derivatives, such as novestrol and norethindrone. Progesterone suppresses ovulation rather than enhancing it, while the estrogen component supports cycle regularity.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct statement is that birth control pills contain a mixture of estrogen and progesterone derivatives.

answer.text: Contain a mixture of estrogen and progesterone derivatives.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMISTRY_IN_EVERYDAY_LIFE_MCQ_Q03 - Properties and classification of analgesic drug aspirin

questiontext.text: Which statement about aspirin is not true

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Classification of Analgesics
Analgesics are neurologically active drugs that relieve pain without causing mental confusion or disturbance of the nervous system. They are divided into non-narcotic (non-addictive) analgesics and narcotic analgesics.

Step 2: Properties and Mechanism of Aspirin
Aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid) is a non-narcotic analgesic. It reduces pain and inflammation by inhibiting prostaglandin synthesis. Aspirin also inhibits platelet aggregation, thereby exhibiting anti-blood clotting activity useful in preventing heart attacks. Narcotic analgesics include opiates such as morphine and codeine.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The untrue statement is that aspirin belongs to narcotic analgesics.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMISTRY_IN_EVERYDAY_LIFE_MCQ_Q04 - Most useful drug classification for medicinal chemists

questiontext.text: The most useful classification of drugs for medicinal chemists is

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Criteria for Drug Classification
Drugs can be classified on the basis of pharmacological effect, drug action on biochemical pathways, chemical structure, or molecular targets.

Step 2: Relevance to Medicinal Chemists
Drugs interact with biological macromolecules such as proteins, nucleic acids, carbohydrates, and lipids, which serve as molecular targets. Classifying drugs on the basis of molecular targets allows medicinal chemists to understand target binding mechanisms and design molecules that selectively bind and regulate these biological targets.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The most useful classification of drugs for medicinal chemists is on the basis of molecular targets.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMISTRY_IN_EVERYDAY_LIFE_MCQ_Q05 - Mechanism of action of tranquilizer drugs

questiontext.text: Which of the following statements is correct?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Role and Nature of Tranquilizers
Tranquilizers are neurologically active, non-narcotic drugs used for treating stress, anxiety, and mild to severe mental disorders. They exert their therapeutic action by affecting the message transfer mechanism from nerve to receptor.

Step 2: Degradation of Noradrenaline
Noradrenaline is a neurotransmitter involved in mood regulation. Low noradrenaline levels diminish signaling in the brain and lead to depression. Certain antidepressant tranquilizers (such as iproniazid and phenelzine) function by inhibiting the enzymes that catalyze the metabolic breakdown of noradrenaline, thereby prolonging receptor activation.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct statement is that some tranquilizers function by inhibiting the enzymes which catalyse the degradation of noradrenaline.

answer.text: Some tranquilisers function by inhibiting the enzymes which catalyse the degradation of noradrenaline.
Transquilisers are chemical compounds that do not affect the message transfer from nerve to receptor.
Tranquilisers are chemical compounds that can relieve pain and fever.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMISTRY_IN_EVERYDAY_LIFE_MCQ_Q06 - Historical medical application of drug Salvarsan

questiontext.text: Salvarsan is arsenic containing drug which was first used for the treatment of

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Historical Development
Paul Ehrlich developed the antimicrobial drug Salvarsan (arsphenamine), an organoarsenic compound with selective toxicity against pathogenic microorganisms.

Step 2: Therapeutic Target Disease
Salvarsan was the first modern chemical therapeutic agent synthesized specifically for the treatment of syphilis, a venereal disease caused by the spirochete bacterium Treponema pallidum.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Salvarsan was first used for the treatment of syphilis.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMISTRY_IN_EVERYDAY_LIFE_MCQ_Q07 - Activity spectrum of narrow spectrum antibiotics

questiontext.text: A narrow spectrum antibiotic is active against

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Definition of Antibiotic Spectrum
The spectrum of an antibiotic describes the diversity of bacterial strains sensitive to that particular antibiotic agent.

Step 2: Differentiation of Spectrum Categories
Broad spectrum antibiotics are effective against a wide range of both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria. Narrow spectrum antibiotics are active mainly against either Gram-positive or Gram-negative bacteria (for example, penicillin G). Limited spectrum antibiotics are effective against only a single organism or specific disease.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
A narrow spectrum antibiotic is active against Gram-positive or Gram-negative bacteria.

answer.text: both gram positive and gram negative bacteria.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMISTRY_IN_EVERYDAY_LIFE_MCQ_Q08 - Drug class producing central antidepressant action

questiontext.text: The compound that causes general antidepressant action on the central nervous system belongs to the class of

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Neurologically Active Drug Categories
Neurologically active drugs alter neurochemical signaling and include tranquilizers and analgesics.

Step 2: Classification of Antidepressants
Tranquilizers are chemical agents used to treat anxiety, stress, tension, and affective mood disorders. Compounds that exert a general antidepressant effect on the central nervous system by improving mood and emotional balance belong to the class of tranquilizers.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The compound belongs to the class of tranquilizers.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMISTRY_IN_EVERYDAY_LIFE_MCQ_Q09 - Antiseptic additive compound used in soaps

questiontext.text: Compound which is added to soap to impart antiseptic properties is

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Functional Roles of Soap Additives
Sodium laurylsulphate and sodium dodecylbenzenesulphonate are synthetic anionic detergents, whereas rosin is a natural resin added to soaps to form sodium rosinate that lathers readily.

Step 2: Antiseptic Impartation
Bithionol (bithional) is a bis-phenol derivative added specifically to toilet soaps to impart antiseptic properties and counteract bacterial growth on the skin.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The compound added to soap to impart antiseptic properties is bithional.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMISTRY_IN_EVERYDAY_LIFE_MCQ_Q10 - Pharmacological classification and action of Equanil

questiontext.text: Equanil is

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Therapeutic Action of Equanil
Equanil is a medication commonly administered to alleviate mild emotional tension, depression, and high blood pressure.

Step 2: Pharmacological Class
Because of its calming action on the central nervous system without causing sleepiness, Equanil is categorized as a tranquilizer.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Equanil is a tranquilizer.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMISTRY_IN_EVERYDAY_LIFE_MCQ_Q11 - Compound that enhances soap lathering property

questiontext.text: Which of the following enhances leathering property of soap?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Chemistry of Soap Additives
Different inorganic and organic builders and additives are mixed with soaps to modify their physical properties.

Step 2: Origin of Enhanced Lathering
A gum called rosin is added to toilet and shaving soaps during saponification, yielding sodium rosinate upon reacting with alkali. Sodium rosinate lathers abundantly and strongly enhances the lathering (leathering) property of the soap.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Sodium rosinate enhances the leathering property of soap.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMISTRY_IN_EVERYDAY_LIFE_MCQ_Q12 - Function of glycerol additive in shaving soap

questiontext.text: Glycerol is added to soap. It functions

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Purpose of Glycerol in Shaving Formulations
Shaving soaps produce lather that must remain hydrated on the face during the shaving process.

Step 2: Hygroscopic Action of Glycerol
Glycerol is a trihydroxy alcohol that possesses humectant properties, allowing it to hold moisture and prevent rapid drying of the lather.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Glycerol functions to prevent rapid drying.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMISTRY_IN_EVERYDAY_LIFE_MCQ_Q13 - Chemical formula of liquid dishwashing detergent

questiontext.text: Which of the following is an example of liquid dishwashing detergent?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Classification of Synthetic Detergents
Synthetic detergents are categorized into anionic detergents (carrying a negative surface-active ion), cationic detergents (carrying a positive surface-active ion), and non-ionic detergents (carrying no electrical charge).

Step 2: Chemical Nature of Liquid Dishwashing Detergents
Liquid dishwashing detergents are non-ionic detergents. They remove grease and oily stains by forming micelles without generating free ions in aqueous medium. A prime example of a non-ionic detergent is the polyoxyethylene derivative of an alkylphenol: \(\mathrm{C}_9\mathrm{H}_{19}\text{---}\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_4\text{---}\mathrm{O}\text{---}(\mathrm{CH}_2\text{---}\mathrm{CH}_2\text{---}\mathrm{O})_5\text{---}\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{OH}\).

Step 3: Evaluation of Other Detergent Classes
Sodium alkylsulphates such as \(\mathrm{CH}_3(\mathrm{CH}_2)_{10}\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{OSO}_3^-\mathrm{Na}^+\) and sodium alkylarylsulphonates are anionic detergents used in laundry soaps and toothpastes, while quaternary ammonium halides are cationic detergents with germicidal properties used in hair conditioners.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The structure \(\mathrm{C}_9\mathrm{H}_{19}\text{---}\mathrm{C}_6\mathrm{H}_4\text{---}\mathrm{O}\text{---}(\mathrm{CH}_2\text{---}\mathrm{CH}_2\text{---}\mathrm{O})_5\text{---}\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{CH}_2\mathrm{OH}\) represents the liquid dishwashing detergent.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMISTRY_IN_EVERYDAY_LIFE_MCQ_Q14 - Preparation of detergents using polyethyleneglycol units

questiontext.text: Polyethyleneglycols are used in the preparation of which type of detergents?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Structure of Non-ionic Detergents
Non-ionic detergents are synthetic surfactants that do not possess any net ionic charge in their molecular architecture.

Step 2: Synthesis Involving Polyethyleneglycols
Non-ionic detergents are prepared by esterification or condensation of long-chain fatty acids (such as stearic acid) or alkylphenols with polyethyleneglycols, generating ether-alcohol chains that provide the hydrophilic moiety.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Polyethyleneglycols are used in the preparation of non-ionic detergents.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMISTRY_IN_EVERYDAY_LIFE_MCQ_Q15 - Target molecules for drug function in body

questiontext.text: Which of the following is not a target molecule for drug function in body?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Definition of Drug Targets
Drug targets are biological macromolecules in the body that interact with pharmacological drugs to trigger physiological responses.

Step 2: Macromolecular Nature of Drug Targets
Proteins (acting as enzymes or receptors), carbohydrates, lipids, and nucleic acids are macromolecular targets with which drugs bind. Vitamins are essential micronutrients rather than macromolecular drug target structures.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Vitamins are not target molecules for drug function in the body.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMISTRY_IN_EVERYDAY_LIFE_MCQ_Q16 - Characteristics and bonding of enzyme inhibitors

questiontext.text: Which of the following statements is not true about enzyme inhibitors?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Function of Enzyme Inhibitors
Enzyme inhibitors block the catalytic action of enzymes by preventing substrate binding or by altering enzyme conformation, functioning competitively or non-competitively.

Step 2: Nature of Enzyme-Inhibitor Interaction
Under typical therapeutic conditions, inhibitors bind reversibly to enzymes via weak non-covalent forces such as hydrogen bonding, van der Waals interactions, dipole-dipole attractions, or ionic interactions. The formation of a strong covalent bond results in irreversible, permanent blocking of the active site (enzyme poisoning), which is not the general mode of action of enzyme inhibitors.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The statement that generally a strong covalent bond is formed between an inhibitor and an enzyme is not true.

answer.text: Inhibit the catalytic activity of the enzyme.
Generally a strong covalent bond is formed between an inhibitor and an enzyme.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMISTRY_IN_EVERYDAY_LIFE_MCQ_Q17 - Thermal stability and calories of artificial sweeteners

questiontext.text: Which of the following chemicals can be added for sweetening of food items at cooking temperature and does not provide calories?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Caloric Value of Sweeteners
Natural carbohydrates such as sucrose and glucose deliver calories upon metabolic oxidation.

Step 2: Thermal Stability of Calorie-Free Sweeteners
Aspartame decomposes at elevated cooking temperatures, restricting its application solely to chilled foods and soft drinks. Sucralose (trichlorosucrose, printed as Sucrolose) does not provide calories and remains thermally stable at baking and cooking temperatures.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Sucrolose can be added for sweetening food items at cooking temperature without providing calories.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMISTRY_IN_EVERYDAY_LIFE_MCQ_Q18 - Food additives that do not enhance nutritional value

questiontext.text: Which of the following will not enhance nutritional value of food?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Definition of Nutritional Supplements
Nutritional additives directly augment the dietary and biological value of food by providing essential elements and nutrients, such as minerals, vitamins, and amino acids.

Step 2: Role of Artificial Sweeteners
Artificial sweeteners are non-nutritive additives that provide sweetness to food without contributing any calories, minerals, or nutrients, so they do not enhance the nutritional value of food.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Artificial sweeteners will not enhance the nutritional value of food.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMISTRY_IN_EVERYDAY_LIFE_MCQ_Q19 - Incorrect statements about cell membrane receptor proteins

questiontext.text:
Note : In the following questions two or more options may be correct.

Which of the following statements are incorrect about receptor proteins?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Structural Orientation of Receptors
Receptor proteins are embedded within the lipid bilayer of cell membranes in such a way that their binding (active) site projects into the extracellular fluid on the outside of the cell, rather than the interior region.

Step 2: Conformational Dynamics Upon Messenger Binding
When a chemical messenger binds to the exterior binding site, the receptor protein undergoes an induced change in its shape (conformation) to propagate the chemical message across the membrane and into the cell interior.

Step 3: Verification of Incorrect Statements
Consequently, the statements claiming that the active site opens on the inside region of the cell and that the receptor shape does not change during attachment of the messenger are incorrect.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The incorrect statements are that the active site of receptor proteins opens on the inside region of the cell, and that the shape of the receptor does not change during attachment of the messenger.

answer.text: Majority of receptor proteins are embedded in the cell membranes.
The active site of receptor proteins opens on the inside region of the cell.
Chemical messengers are received at the binding sites of receptor proteins.
Shape of receptor doesn't change during attachment of messenger.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMISTRY_IN_EVERYDAY_LIFE_MCQ_Q20 - Substances evaluated regarding food preservative roles

questiontext.text:
Note : In the following questions two or more options may be correct.

Which of the following are not used as food preservatives?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle of Food Preservation
Food preservatives inhibit microbial growth to prevent decomposition and spoilage. Common traditional preservatives include table salt, cane sugar, and vegetable oils, while chemical preservatives include sodium benzoate and salts of propanoic or sorbic acid.

Step 2: NCERT Curriculum and Chemical Evaluation
In the NCERT Exemplar curriculum key for this question, table salt and cane sugar are specifically designated. Chemically, sodium hydrogencarbonate functions as an antacid and leavening agent rather than a preservative.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
Table salt and cane sugar are the designated choices in accordance with the curriculum answer key.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMISTRY_IN_EVERYDAY_LIFE_MCQ_Q21 - Identification of compounds possessing antiseptic properties

questiontext.text:
Note : In the following questions two or more options may be correct.

Compounds with antiseptic properties are

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Antiseptics are antimicrobial substances suitable for topical application to living tissues without causing toxic injury.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Given Compounds
Iodoform (\(\mathrm{CHI}_3\)) acts as an antiseptic on wounds due to the slow release of free iodine. A dilute aqueous solution of boric acid is commonly used as a mild antiseptic for ophthalmic use (washing eyes).

Step 3: Characterization of Other Substances
Chloroform (\(\mathrm{CHCl}_3\)) was historically utilized as a general anesthetic, and an aqueous chlorine solution at a concentration of 0.2 to 0.4 ppm acts as a disinfectant for water treatment.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The compounds possessing antiseptic properties are \(\mathrm{CHI}_3\) and boric acid.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMISTRY_IN_EVERYDAY_LIFE_MCQ_Q22 - Pharmacological properties and nature of barbiturates

questiontext.text:
Note : In the following questions two or more options may be correct.

Which of the following statements are correct about barbiturates?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Nature and Classification of Barbiturates
Barbiturates (derivatives of barbituric acid including veronal, luminal, amytal, and seconal) belong to the pharmacological category of tranquilizers.

Step 2: Physiological Effects
They exert depressive effects on the central nervous system that induce sleep, classifying them as hypnotics (sleep-producing agents). They are not analgesics and do not relieve pain selectively without disturbing the nervous system.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct statements are that barbiturates are hypnotics or sleep producing agents, and that they are tranquilizers.

answer.text: Pain reducing without disturbing the nervous system.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMISTRY_IN_EVERYDAY_LIFE_MCQ_Q23 - Chemical identification of sulpha antimicrobial drugs

questiontext.text:
Note : In the following questions two or more options may be correct.

Which of the following are sulpha drugs?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Structural Feature of Sulpha Drugs
Sulpha drugs are synthetic antibacterial agents structurally related to sulphanilamide (\(p\text{-aminobenzenesulphonamide}\)).

Step 2: Evaluation of the Compounds
Prontosil was the pioneer azo-dye compound that breaks down in the body to produce active sulphanilamide, functioning as a sulpha drug. Sulphapyridine is a direct sulfonamide derivative belonging to the sulpha drug group. Salvarsan is an organoarsenic antibiotic, and Nardil (phenelzine) is an antidepressant.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The sulpha drugs are sulphapyridine and prontosil.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMISTRY_IN_EVERYDAY_LIFE_MCQ_Q24 - Identification of clinical antidepressant drug compounds

questiontext.text:
Note : In the following questions two or more options may be correct.

Which of the following are antidepressants?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Role of Antidepressant Drugs
Antidepressants are therapeutic agents designed to counteract depression by inhibiting enzymes that degrade mood-regulating neurotransmitters (such as noradrenaline) or by mitigating nervous tension.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Compounds
Iproniazid and phenelzine (Nardil) inhibit the enzyme monoamine oxidase, thereby raising noradrenaline levels to relieve depression. Equanil is also utilized in controlling depression and hypertension. Salvarsan is an arsenic-containing antimicrobial agent used for syphilis, not an antidepressant.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The antidepressants are iproniazid, phenelzine, and equanil.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMISTRY_IN_EVERYDAY_LIFE_MCQ_Q25 - Incorrect statements about characteristics of penicillin

questiontext.text:
Note : In the following questions two or more options may be correct.

Which of the following statements are incorrect about penicillin?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Origin and Synthetic Modifications of Penicillin
Penicillin was originally derived from the fungus Penicillium notatum, and ampicillin is a semisynthetic modification of penicillin.

Step 2: Bactericidal Action and Spectrum
Penicillin exerts a bactericidal (bacterial-killing) effect rather than a bacteriostatic (growth-inhibiting) effect. Moreover, natural penicillin has a narrow spectrum of antimicrobial action, being effective primarily against Gram-positive bacteria, unlike broad-spectrum agents that attack diverse Gram-positive and Gram-negative pathogens.

Step 3: Identification of Incorrect Statements
The statements asserting that penicillin has a bacteriostatic effect and that it is a broad spectrum antibiotic are incorrect.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The incorrect statements are that penicillin has a bacteriostatic effect and that it is a broad spectrum antibiotic.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_CHEMISTRY_IN_EVERYDAY_LIFE_MCQ_Q26 - Chemical compounds administered as medical antacids

questiontext.text:
Note : In the following questions two or more options may be correct.

Which of the following compounds are administered as antacids?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Antacid Properties and Mechanism
Antacids are mild basic substances taken to neutralize excessive hydrochloric acid in stomach secretions without causing mucosal irritation.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Compounds
Sodium hydrogencarbonate (\(\mathrm{NaHCO}_3\)) and magnesium hydroxide (\(\mathrm{Mg(OH)}_2\), milk of magnesia) are widely administered antacids. Sodium carbonate is excessively basic and corrosive, while aluminium carbonate is unstable and not used as an antacid.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The compounds administered as antacids are sodium hydrogencarbonate and magnesium hydroxide.
